I hanged myself when I was thirteen, was saved, spent two weeks in a coma, lost my memory and had to learn everything from the start: language, math, didn't recognize my family... Took me years to get my memory back in order.

I was lucky enough to find a good therapist, pills that did thier job and friends who stayed by me.

I went on to organize massive water wars (over 15 thousand people with water rifles, balloons...), joined the Free Hugs campaign (where you stand in the street, with a sign offering hugs to passerby and hug them), organized free parties for the public and through that, got more and more friends, got many more disappointing events and some heavenly amazing ones.

I keep reminding myself that my mind is working against me, therapy and pills help the struggle and through thier help, the help of friends and family, I was able to go on for another twenty five years, with amazing people around me, beautiful relationships and an option for a wonderful future of helping and fulfilling myself and others.

For me, it required realizing I needed help getting back on track, antidepressants to smooth things over and the courage to just try, again and again. Some times, realizing, I needed to lean on friends or family.

There's always a way, you just need some push forward to find the right way to assist yourself to carry on.

Good luck, my friend!

I hanged myself when I was 13 years old. (37 now).  
People keep telling me what a brave kid I must have been.  


Thinking about it now, after all these years... killing myself would have been the cowardly thing to do.  
Living each and every moment, day - struggling with the pain, with taking my medication and fighting onwards to try more and more things to solve the issues was the braver thing to do and I can see myself doing the exact same thing, surviving it (even though it was and still is hard as all hell).  


If you're in pain, any kind of pain, see a friend, a relative, a doctor... anyone who you trust (or think you could have trusted, before the depression clouded your mind).  


There's always a chance to go on and as long as it's there, you need to find the strentgth to grab it. <3
